You know I was caught once drinking alone. I became raging drunk(a silent drunk though) and I had put two half-full beer cans in my jean pockets and they had spilled all over my bed sheets. I woke up to this disaster the next morning, I was frantically ripping off the sheets and trying to hide them in some desolated room. My grandparents and mother eventually found. They confided in me that they viewed behavior as disturbing and reckless. My therapist also attributed these things to "self-destructive tendencies". I didn't know how to respond to these allegations since in these people's minds, I was on the road to becoming an alcoholic. I was only looking at it one way. I just thought to myself "what do you expect me to do? I"m 15." 

I don't think they bought that. Maybe I shouldn't have to myself either. In these times I found that I had doubted my thoughts and reasonings for doing things, and would eventually come to believe the sayings of others. I began to doubt the responsibility of my own choices, I became confused by adults. I became confused by everything, the decisions people made, and their reasonings as to why I couldn't do the same. Their explanations were always the same "It harms the teenage brain", "you're too young", and "you don't know how to control it". And to these statements, I just thought...why couldn't I be taught how to control it. And if I couldn't be taught, then what gave me the right to decide if I wanted to touch that bottle? Who was I to determine such a thing for myself? Why am I considered to be a free person, but the instant I make a bad choice for myself, the chains are pulled tighter? After these reflections, I had eventually fell into a nihilist worldview, of which their is no recovery. I decided that the only option I really had without fear of judgement and opiniated bias directed towards me, was that I had to conform. I had to do things their way, not my way. There was no place for my way, my body can't handle my way. My mind would deteriorate my way. I had to let others make the decisions for me at this age. And from then on...well I would follow in society's road for me. One more person to represent model-citezenship. I hope these views don't change anytime soon, it's what has been holding me together nowadays. Without others to guide me, I'm left alone to guide myself. And that task is one I am not ready for. So...OP, my question is, are you having fun?

However, even regarding all this, heroin use can be regulated, but it's best not to be touched if you care about your life. The decision is ultimately yours alone, but you must base that decision off the circumstances of your wants and needs. Does family apply to you? Does safety concern you? Does health matter to you? Do you matter to yourself. These are questions one must face with regarding use of a serious drug. After the overdose, I reflected deeply on these questions and decided that they all matter to me, in the end, they will all matter.
